# Maggakathā (Ps 1.9)

**ID:** Ps 1.9
**Section:** Paṭisambhidāmagga (ps)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Maggakathā* ("Discussion of the Path", Ps 1.9) is the ninth treatise of the first division (*Mahāvagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*. The text presents an analytical exposition of the four supramundane paths and the eight path-factors (*magg'aṅga*), integrating all seven standard sets of qualities leading to awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) [Gethin 2001]. Unlike related chapters in the work (such as the *Ānāpānassatikathā*) where items are framed through their functional purpose (*attha*), the *Maggakathā* defines the path-factors directly as facets of the path itself—such as "the path of seeing is right view" (*dassana-maggo sammā-diṭṭhi*) and "the path of directing [thought] is right thought" (*abhiropana-maggo sammā-saṅkappo*)—applying this model consistently across awakening-factors, spiritual faculties, and powers [Gethin 2001].

 Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus documents 614 shared passages across 34 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of these correspondences occur internally within the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, notably with the *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), *Virāgakathā* (Ps 2.5), *Abhisamayakathā* (Ps 3.3), *Ānāpānassatikathā* (Ps 1.3), and *Indriyakathā* (Ps 1.4) [DharmaNexus]. Substantial shared phraseology is also identified in the Abhidhamma's *Yamaka* (*Pahīnavāra*, Ya 7.2.5), Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga*, the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali literature, DharmaNexus automatically aligns a passage (§8.2_5) with the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā Lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* [DharmaNexus].
